quarterly_data.signal: CEO George Kurian quantified the flash-vs-disk cost gap driving a mix shift back to hard disk: NetApp's disk-based systems have started to show growth and he sees 'strong uptake through the rest of the year as the cost of flash becomes 15 to 20 times the cost of disk.' NetApp is giving customers tools to keep high-cost flash only for data that needs it and to automate movement of colder data out of flash-based systems into cheaper disk-based configurations - a large part of the data in an all-flash array is in fact cold.
quarterly_data.figure: the cost of flash becomes 15 to 20 times the cost of disk

quarterly_data.signal: NAND and hard-disk procurement behind the raised FY2027 guide: Kurian said NetApp works with suppliers on 'a broad range of commercial vehicles, including buying in the open market as well as through Long-Term Agreements to assure access to available supply at competitive cost structures', and that suppliers prefer that range of tools. He pointed to the balance sheet: inventory was up in the quarter because NetApp wants adequate inventory on hand to meet demand.

Sovereign-cloud position: 'six of the eight largest cloud providers in France have NetApp as their infrastructure' - domestic cloud providers - and NetApp is part of several sovereign build-outs in Europe. Kurian said the sovereign push is growing worldwide because AI is treated as a national security priority, and that NetApp's differentiation is letting customers use hyperscaler AI platforms while keeping private data storage and data management on NetApp.
quarterly_data.figure: six of the eight largest cloud providers in France have NetApp as their infrastructure

quarterly_data.signal: Next catalyst - NetApp INSIGHT: Kurian pre-announced 'even more advancements for the really high end of the NeoCloud for training and this frontier models use cases coming up at Insight' and later 'product announcements at Insight for super high-scale frontier lab kind of training environments', which if successful 'will also bring us a new class of customers'. The existing AFX disaggregated platform (large enterprises and some NeoClouds) is going through customer certification with good uptake.

Customer behaviour under component inflation is running counter to the historical pattern: NetApp planned for a normal pattern of X new use cases and a decrease in refresh/infrastructure upgrades when prices rise, but is 'seeing infrastructure upgrades way above normal pattern' and 'new use cases also way above normal pattern', which Kurian reads as a secular spending shift toward the storage category. Separately, NetApp is working with several clients on hybrid compute landscapes where they provision compute in the cloud as a risk mitigation strategy for not having access to supply chain components for their own data centers.

connects_to.relationship: NetApp storage under Google Distributed Cloud - Google AI stack with NetApp private data storage in disconnected/sovereign environments

contracts.signal: CEO George Kurian on the expanded Google Distributed Cloud relationship: 'in the Google Distributed Cloud architecture, they are bringing the Google AI stack with NetApp storage to a private, disconnected environment in customers', and NetApp sees more and more of those sovereign use cases, not only with Google but with other cloud providers. He also cited Vertex from Google as one of the hyperscaler AI platforms NetApp connects its public-cloud offerings to.

connects_to.relationship: Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP - NetApp's first-party storage service on AWS

contracts.signal: Kurian: NetApp continues to invest in connecting its public-cloud offerings to the hyperscalers' AI platforms 'like Bedrock from Amazon or Vertex from Google or Azure AI Studio from Microsoft', and 'innovations that we introduced a couple of quarters ago with Amazon' saw super strong uptake in the quarter - life sciences customers running molecular analysis and diagnostics tool chains, serverless functions and LLM tools against NetApp data infrastructure, use cases NetApp would not have won on-prem.
